---
title: "Known discrepancies"
subtitle: "Clocks whose circulating coefficients differ from what their paper describes"
---

Some clocks are scored from coefficients that differ from what their paper describes: a feature
count, a changed statistic, a constant. FALCONAge scores the coefficients listed here,
records the difference in the clock's registry entry, and raises it as a warning on every run
that scores the clock, so it appears in `warnings.csv` and the report rather than only here.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: discrepancies -->

22 of the 178 catalogued clocks carry a `known_discrepancies` note: a place where the paper, its coefficients and the implementations in circulation disagree. Each is raised as a warning at score time.

| Clock | The disagreement |
|:---------|:----------------------------|
| `bocklandt` | The paper describes a 2-CpG model; the coefficient set in circulation carries 1. Which probe was dropped is not documented upstream, so this is not the published model. |
| `bohlin` | The paper reports 96 CpGs; the coefficient set in circulation carries 251. Scores here will match other packages and not the figures printed in the paper. |
| `cvdwesterman` | The paper reports 1,305 CpGs; the coefficient set in circulation carries 235. Expect disagreement with any value quoted from the paper. |
| `mccartneyalcohol`, `mccartneybmi`, `mccartneybodyfat`, `mccartneyeducation`, `mccartneyhdlcholesterol`, `mccartneyldlcholesterol`, `mccartneysmoking`, `mccartneytotalcholesterol`, `mccartneytotalhdlratio`, `mccartneywhr` | The paper defines this predictor as a weighted sum of beta values and applies no link function; the ROC analysis it reports dichotomises the phenotype, not the score. Packages that pass the sum through a sigmoid report a different number. The scale is relative_score, whose legal operations are correlate and rank, and a sigmoid is monotone, so no permitted result changes either way. |
| `phenoage` | Two constants circulate in the divisor of the Gompertz inversion: 0.090165, printed in Levine 2018 Supplement 1, and 0.09165, printed in Liu et al. 2018 (PLoS Med). FALCONAge uses 0.090165, the value BioAge corrected to in April 2026. Code still using 0.09165 differs by several years on the same input. |
| `phenoage` | Levine 2018 Table 1 prints alkaline phosphatase as 0.0019; Liu et al. 2018 print 0.00188, and BioAge carries the fit at full precision (0.001868778, every weight rounding to Table 1). FALCONAge uses Table 1 as printed, a mean 0.074 years above the full-precision fit on NHANES III; phenoage(df, coefficients='bioage') uses BioAge's. |
| `phenoage` | BioAge enters CRP as log(1 + CRP), its lncrp, where the paper uses log(CRP). On NHANES III that puts BioAge's phenoage0 a mean 1.50 years above the paper's formula (SD 0.45, more at low CRP; n = 8,924). FALCONAge follows the paper; phenoage(df, crp_transform='log1p', coefficients='bioage') reproduces phenoage0 exactly. |
| `senchronoage`, `sencultureage`, `senmortalityage` | The upstream README's feature count disagrees with the coefficient object it ships. The registry follows the coefficient file, because that is what scores. |
| `weidner` | The third site is a substitution. The paper's gamma is not cg17861230 but an unnamed CpG upstream of it, measured by pyrosequencing and better correlated with age; no array id was ever published for it. Every array implementation of this clock, including this one, puts cg17861230 in its place, and gamma carries 164.7 of the model against 26.4 and 23.7 for the two genuine probes. Treat the result as the published model evaluated on a near neighbour. |
| `yingadaptage`, `yingdamage` | Scored across three healthy cohorts in the FALCONAge corpus, this clock's median offset against chronological age swings 162 years between datasets while Horvath2013's swings 15; DamAge and AdaptAge move as near mirror images (r = -0.975) and the swing in their sum is only 33, so the cause is one dataset-level shift amplified by their opposing intercepts of +543.43 and -511.97 rather than a fault in either. The slope against age is sound (0.967 pooled for DamAge). The scale is therefore age_years_relative: the residual and group differences are defined, predicted-minus-chronological is not. |
| `yingadaptage` | The paper reports 1,000 CpGs; the coefficient set carries 999. The same off-by-one appears in all three Ying clocks, consistent with the paper's total counting an intercept row as a feature. |
| `yingcausage` | The paper reports 586 CpGs; the coefficient set carries 585. The same off-by-one appears in all three Ying clocks, consistent with the paper's total counting an intercept row as a feature. |
| `yingdamage` | The paper reports 1,090 CpGs; the coefficient set carries 1,089. The same off-by-one appears in all three Ying clocks, consistent with the paper's total counting an intercept row as a feature. |
| `zhangmortality` | The paper defines this as an integer count of markers past quartile thresholds; the implementations in circulation compute a continuous weighted sum. They are different statistics, and the continuous form has no published cut-points. FALCONAge scores the continuous sum of the LASSO Cox weights, a log hazard (scale_type mortality_log_hazard), not the count. |

<!-- END GENERATED: discrepancies -->

The table is generated from the registry by `docs/build_catalogue.py`: `reg.get(id).known_discrepancies`
returns the full text, and `res.manifest["warnings"]` carries whichever of them fired on your run.
The Ying clocks additionally carry a measured cohort-offset note, which is why they sit on
`age_years_relative` rather than `age_years`, [What the calibration found, and what it turned into](../methods/uncertainty.qmd#what-the-calibration-found-and-what-it-turned-into).
